Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 45, verse 14–22:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive...﴾ [the verse]. Regarding its occasion of revelation there are four reports.

The first: they descended at the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, at a well called "al-Muraysi'" (al-Muraysi'). ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent a servant (ghulam) of his to draw water, and he was slow in returning. When he came, [ʿAbd Allah] said to him: "What delayed you?" He said: "The servant of ʿUmar. He did not leave anyone drawing water until he had filled the water-skins of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the water-skins of Abu Bakr, and he filled [water] for his master (mawla)." ʿAbd Allah said: "Our likeness and theirs is nothing but as it was said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" His saying reached ʿUmar, so he took up his sword intending to go to him, and this verse was revealed. Narrated by ʿAtaʾ from Ibn ʿAbbas.

(p-358) The second: [it was revealed] when there was revealed: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245], a Jew in Medina called Finhas said: "The Lord of Muhammad has become needy." When ʿUmar heard of this, he took up his sword and set out in pursuit of him, and Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with this verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent for ʿUmar, and when he came, he said: "O ʿUmar, put down your sword," and recited the verse to him. Narrated by Maymun ibn Mihran from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: that some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Makkah were under severe harm from the polytheists before they were commanded to fight, so they complained of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed. Said by al-Qurazi and al-Suddi.

The fourth: that a man from the disbelievers of Quraysh insulted ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, so ʿUmar intended to strike him, and this verse was revealed. Said by Muqatil.

The meaning of the verse: Say to those who believe: "Forgive," but it is phrased in the form of a condition and a consequence, like His saying: ﴿Say to My servants who believe: let them establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim: 31], and the explanation of this has already passed.

His saying: ﴿those who do not expect﴾ means: they do not fear the events (waqai') of Allah among the bygone nations, because they do not believe in Him, so they do not fear His punishment. It was said: they do not know whether the blessings of Allah upon them are [from Him] or not. The explanation of the meaning of "the Days of Allah" has already passed in Surah [Ibrahim: 5].

(p-359) * Section

The majority of exegetes hold that this verse is abrogated (mansukh), because it contains the command to turn away from the polytheists. They differed regarding its abrogating verse (nasikh) in three views.

The first: [it is] His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5]. Narrated by Maʿmar from Qatadah.

The second: it is His saying in [al-Anfal: 57]: ﴿So if you overcome them in war﴾, and His saying in [Bara'ah: 36]: ﴿and fight the polytheists all together﴾. Narrated by Saʿid from Qatadah.

The third: [it is] His saying: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought because they have been wronged﴾ [al-Hajj: 39]. Said by Abu Salih.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that He may recompense a people﴾. Ibn ʿAmir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "linajziya" with the nun, "qawman" meaning the disbelievers, so it is as if He said: do not requite them yourselves, that We may requite them.

What follows this has already been discussed [al-Isra': 7], up to His saying: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Book﴾, meaning the Torah, ﴿and the judgment﴾, which is understanding of the Book, ﴿and We provided them with good things﴾, meaning manna and quail, ﴿and We preferred them over the worlds﴾, meaning the worlds of their time.

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾. Regarding this there are two views.

One: the clarification of the lawful and the unlawful, said by al-Suddi.
